title: Banda’s Defiant Reply and the Opening of the Tat Khalsa Estrangement

blocks.text: The letter reaches Banda, but the hoped-for submission never arrives. In his reply he refuses the summons, argues that the Mughals would never spare him, and bluntly says, I am no longer the Guru’s Sikh.

His answer sharpens the break by presenting himself as a Bairagi Vaishnav with his own sovereignty and public formula of victory. What the court hoped would be reconciliation instead becomes proof that Banda now speaks in a separate political and spiritual register.

This page therefore functions as a transition rather than a simple refusal. Banda’s defiant reply immediately opens the Tat Khalsa estrangement, because slanderers seize on the letter to claim that even the Guru Mother cannot draw him back.
